351: 
352: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
353: verified by the defined `verify` option. The `status` property is
354: set to `403`, the `type` property is set to `'entity.verify.failed'`, and the
355: `body` property is set to the entity value that failed verification.
356: 
357: ### request aborted
358: 
359: This error will occur when the request is aborted by the client before reading
360: the body has finished. The `received` property will be set to the number of
361: bytes received before the request was aborted and the `expected` property is
362: set to the number of expected bytes. The `status` property is set to `400`
363: and `type` property is set to `'request.aborted'`.
364: 
365: ### request entity too large
366: 
367: This error will occur when the request body's size is larger than the "limit"
368: option. The `limit` property will be set to the byte limit and the `length`
369: property will be set to the request body's length. The `status` property is
370: set to `413` and the `type` property is set to `'entity.too.large'`.
371: 
372: ### request size did not match content length
373: 
374: This error will occur when the request's length did not match the length from
375: the `Content-Length` header. This typically occurs when the request is malformed,
376: typically when the `Content-Length` header was calculated based on characters
377: instead of bytes. The `status` property is set to `400` and the `type` property
378: is set to `'request.size.invalid'`.
379: 
380: ### stream encoding should not be set
381: 
382: This error will occur when something called the `req.setEncoding` method prior
383: to this middleware. This module operates directly on bytes only and you cannot
384: call `req.setEncoding` when using this module. The `status` property is set to
385: `500` and the `type` property is set to `'stream.encoding.set'`.
386: 
387: ### stream is not readable
388: 
389: This error will occur when the request is no longer readable when this middleware
390: attempts to read it. This typically means something other than a middleware from
391: this module read the request body already and the middleware was also configured to
392: read the same request. The `status` property is set to `500` and the `type`
393: property is set to `'stream.not.readable'`.
394: 
395: ### too many parameters
396: 
397: This error will occur when the content of the request exceeds the configured
398: `parameterLimit` for the `urlencoded` parser. The `status` property is set to
399: `413` and the `type` property is set to `'parameters.too.many'`.
400: 
401: ### unsupported charset "BOGUS"
402: 
403: This error will occur when the request had a charset parameter in the
404: `Content-Type` header, but the `iconv-lite` module does not support it OR the
405: parser does not support it. The charset is contained in the message as well
406: as in the `charset` property. The `status` property is set to `415`, the
407: `type` property is set to `'charset.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property
408: is set to the charset that is unsupported.

411: 
412: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that

2.4.0
=====

* Security fix for [GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828](https://github.com/expressjs/body-parser/security/advisories/GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828) (CVE-2026-111181)
* feat: add `zstd` content-encoding support (#586)
  * Requires Node.js `^22.15.0` or `>=23.8.0`; older versions keep returning `415` for `zstd` encoded bodies
* fix: avoid mutating the parser options and the request object while reading the body (#742, #750)
* perf(json): avoid first-char regex for direct JSON bodies (#744)
* deps:
  * content-type@^2.1.0
  * iconv-lite^0.7.3
  * qs@^6.16.1

2.3.0
=====

* Security fix for [GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6](https://github.com/expressjs/body-parser/security/advisories/GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6)
* fix: use static exports instead of lazy getters to improve ESM compatibility
* feat: add subpath exports for individual parsers
* fix: improve `limit` option validation (#698)
  * Invalid `limit` values (e.g. unparseable strings or `NaN`) now throw instead of being silently ignored, which previously disabled size limit enforcement
  * `null` and `undefined` fall back to the default 100kb limit
* deps:
  * content-type@^2.0.0
  * http-errors@^2.0.1
  * iconv-lite^0.7.2
  * qs@^6.15.2
  * raw-body@^3.0.2
  * type-is@^2.1.0

##### rawBody

When set to `true`, the raw request body bytes are made available on
`req.rawBody` as a `Buffer`. The bytes are the decompressed body, after any
`Content-Encoding` (such as `gzip`) has been removed, but before the charset
is decoded, so `req.rawBody` retains the original bytes even when `req.body`
is a decoded string (for example, a `latin1` body keeps its `latin1` bytes).
This is useful for verifying request signatures (such as webhook signatures)
over the exact bytes received. Defaults to `false`, in which case
`req.rawBody` is not set. Works together with the `verify` option, and the
bytes remain available even when body parsing fails.

function.name: todowrite
function.description:
Create and maintain a structured task list for the current coding session. Tracks progress, organizes multi-step work, and surfaces status to the user.

## When to use
Use proactively when:
- The task requires 3+ distinct steps or actions (not just 3 tool calls for a single conceptual step)
- The work is non-trivial and benefits from planning
- The user provides multiple tasks (numbered or comma-separated) or explicitly asks for a todo list
- New instructions arrive - capture them as todos
- You start a task - mark it `in_progress` (only one at a time) before working
- You finish a task - mark it `completed` and add any follow-ups discovered during the work

## When NOT to use
Skip when:
- The work is a single, straightforward task (or <3 trivial steps)
- The request is purely informational or conversational
- Tracking adds no organizational value

## States
- `pending` - not started
- `in_progress` - actively working (exactly ONE at a time)
- `completed` - finished successfully
- `cancelled` - no longer needed

## Rules
- Update status in real time; don't batch completions
- Mark `completed` only after the required work is actually done, including any required verification. Never based on intent.
- Keep exactly one `in_progress` while work remains
- If blocked or partial, keep it `in_progress` and add a follow-up todo describing the blocker
- Preserve user-provided commands verbatim (flags, args, order)
- Items should be specific and actionable; break large work into smaller steps

## Examples

Use it:
- "Add a dark mode toggle and run the tests" -> multi-step feature + explicit verification
- "Rename getCwd -> getCurrentWorkingDirectory across the repo" -> grep reveals 15 occurrences in 8 files
- "Implement registration, catalog, cart, checkout" -> multiple complex features

Skip it:
- "How do I print Hello World in Python?" -> informational
- "Add a comment to calculateTotal" -> single edit
- "Run npm install and tell me what happened" -> one command

When in doubt, use it.

81: ### bodyParser.json([options])
82: 
83: Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
84: the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
85: Unicode encoding of the body.
86: 
87: A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
88: object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).
89: 
90: #### Options
91: 
92: The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
93: the following keys:
94: 
95: ##### defaultCharset
96: 
97: Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
98: specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.
99: 
100: ##### inflate
101: 
102: When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
103: `false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.
104: 
105: ##### limit
106: 
107: Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
108: specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
109: [bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
110: to `'100kb'`.
111: 
112: > It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.
113: 
114: ##### reviver
115: 
116: The `reviver` option is passed directly to `JSON.parse` as the second
117: argument. You can find more information on this argument
118: [in the MDN documentation about JSON.parse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/parse#the_reviver_parameter).
119: 
120: ##### strict
121: 
122: When set to `true`, it will only accept arrays and objects; when `false`, it will
123: accept anything `JSON.parse` accepts. Defaults to `true`.
124: 
125: ##### type
126: 
127: The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
128: parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not a
129: function, `type` option is passed directly to the
130: [type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
131: be an extension name (like `json`), a mime type (like `application/json`), or
132: a mime type with a wildcard (like `*/*` or `*/json`). If a function, the `type`
133: option is called as `fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy
134: value. Defaults to `application/json`.
135: 
136: ##### verify
137: 
138: The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
139: where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
140: encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.

By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.

277: ##### parameterLimit
278: 
279: The `parameterLimit` option controls the maximum number of parameters that
280: are allowed in the URL-encoded data. If a request contains more parameters
281: than this value, a 413 will be returned to the client. Defaults to `1000`.
282: 
283: ##### type
284: 
285: The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
286: parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not
287: a function, `type` option is passed directly to the
288: [type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
289: be an extension name (like `urlencoded`), a mime type (like
290: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`), or a mime type with a wildcard (like
291: `*/x-www-form-urlencoded`). If a function, the `type` option is called as
292: `fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy value. Defaults
293: to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.
294: 
295: ##### verify
296: 
297: The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
298: where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
299: encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.
300: 
301: ##### defaultCharset
302: 
303: The default charset to parse as, if not specified in content-type. Must be
304: either `utf-8` or `iso-8859-1`. Defaults to `utf-8`.
305: 
306: ##### charsetSentinel
307: 
308: Whether to let the value of the `utf8` parameter take precedence as the charset
309: selector. It requires the form to contain a parameter named `utf8` with a value
310: of `✓`. Defaults to `false`.
311: 
312: ##### interpretNumericEntities
313: 
314: Whether to decode numeric entities such as `☺` when parsing an iso-8859-1
315: form. Defaults to `false`.
316: 
317: 
318: ##### depth
319: 
320: The `depth` option is used to configure the maximum depth of the `qs` library when `extended` is `true`. This allows you to limit the amount of keys that are parsed and can be useful to prevent certain types of abuse. Defaults to `32`. It is recommended to keep this value as low as possible.
321: 
322: ## Errors
323: 
324: The middlewares provided by this module create errors using the
325: [`http-errors` module](https://www.npmjs.com/package/http-errors). The errors
326: will typically have a `status`/`statusCode` property that contains the suggested
327: HTTP response code, an `expose` property to determine if the `message` property
328: should be displayed to the client, a `type` property to determine the type of
329: error without matching against the `message`, and a `body` property containing
330: the read body, if available.
331: 
332: The following are the common errors created, though any error can come through
333: for various reasons.
334: 
335: ### content encoding unsupported
336: 
337: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
338: contained an encoding but the "inflation" option was set to `false`. The
339: `status` property is set to `415`, the `type` property is set to
340: `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property will be set to the
341: encoding that is unsupported.
342: 
343: ### entity parse failed
344: 
345: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
346: parsed by the middleware. The `status` property is set to `400`, the `type`
347: property is set to `'entity.parse.failed'`, and the `body` property is set to
348: the entity value that failed parsing.
349: 
350: ### entity verify failed
351: 
352: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
353: verified by the defined `verify` option. The `status` property is
354: set to `403`, the `type` property is set to `'entity.verify.failed'`, and the
355: `body` property is set to the entity value that failed verification.
356: 
357: ### request aborted
358: 
359: This error will occur when the request is aborted by the client before reading
360: the body has finished. The `received` property will be set to the number of
361: bytes received before the request was aborted and the `expected` property is
362: set to the number of expected bytes. The `status` property is set to `400`
363: and `type` property is set to `'request.aborted'`.
364: 
365: ### request entity too large
366: 
367: This error will occur when the request body's size is larger than the "limit"
368: option. The `limit` property will be set to the byte limit and the `length`
369: property will be set to the request body's length. The `status` property is
370: set to `413` and the `type` property is set to `'entity.too.large'`.
371: 
372: ### request size did not match content length
373: 
374: This error will occur when the request's length did not match the length from
375: the `Content-Length` header. This typically occurs when the request is malformed,
376: typically when the `Content-Length` header was calculated based on characters
377: instead of bytes. The `status` property is set to `400` and the `type` property
378: is set to `'request.size.invalid'`.
379: 
380: ### stream encoding should not be set
381: 
382: This error will occur when something called the `req.setEncoding` method prior
383: to this middleware. This module operates directly on bytes only and you cannot
384: call `req.setEncoding` when using this module. The `status` property is set to
385: `500` and the `type` property is set to `'stream.encoding.set'`.
386: 
387: ### stream is not readable
388: 
389: This error will occur when the request is no longer readable when this middleware
390: attempts to read it. This typically means something other than a middleware from
391: this module read the request body already and the middleware was also configured to
392: read the same request. The `status` property is set to `500` and the `type`
393: property is set to `'stream.not.readable'`.
394: 
395: ### too many parameters
396: 
397: This error will occur when the content of the request exceeds the configured
398: `parameterLimit` for the `urlencoded` parser. The `status` property is set to
399: `413` and the `type` property is set to `'parameters.too.many'`.
400: 
401: ### unsupported charset "BOGUS"
402: 
403: This error will occur when the request had a charset parameter in the
404: `Content-Type` header, but the `iconv-lite` module does not support it OR the
405: parser does not support it. The charset is contained in the message as well
406: as in the `charset` property. The `status` property is set to `415`, the
407: `type` property is set to `'charset.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property
408: is set to the charset that is unsupported.
409: 
410: ### unsupported content encoding "bogus"
411: 
412: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
413: contained an unsupported encoding. The encoding is contained in the message
414: as well as in the `encoding` property. The `status` property is set to `415`,
415: the `type` property is set to `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `encoding`
416: property is set to the encoding that is unsupported.
417: 
418: ### The input exceeded the depth
419: 
420: This error occurs when using `bodyParser.urlencoded` with the `extended` property set to `true` and the input exceeds the configured `depth` option. The `status` property is set to `400`. It is recommended to review the `depth` option and evaluate if it requires a higher value. With the default `depth` of `32`, an input with 33 or more levels of nesting gets this error.

function.name: todowrite
function.description:
Create and maintain a structured task list for the current coding session. Tracks progress, organizes multi-step work, and surfaces status to the user.

## When to use
Use proactively when:
- The task requires 3+ distinct steps or actions (not just 3 tool calls for a single conceptual step)
- The work is non-trivial and benefits from planning
- The user provides multiple tasks (numbered or comma-separated) or explicitly asks for a todo list
- New instructions arrive - capture them as todos
- You start a task - mark it `in_progress` (only one at a time) before working
- You finish a task - mark it `completed` and add any follow-ups discovered during the work

## When NOT to use
Skip when:
- The work is a single, straightforward task (or <3 trivial steps)
- The request is purely informational or conversational
- Tracking adds no organizational value

## States
- `pending` - not started
- `in_progress` - actively working (exactly ONE at a time)
- `completed` - finished successfully
- `cancelled` - no longer needed

## Rules
- Update status in real time; don't batch completions
- Mark `completed` only after the required work is actually done, including any required verification. Never based on intent.
- Keep exactly one `in_progress` while work remains
- If blocked or partial, keep it `in_progress` and add a follow-up todo describing the blocker
- Preserve user-provided commands verbatim (flags, args, order)
- Items should be specific and actionable; break large work into smaller steps

## Examples

Use it:
- "Add a dark mode toggle and run the tests" -> multi-step feature + explicit verification
- "Rename getCwd -> getCurrentWorkingDirectory across the repo" -> grep reveals 15 occurrences in 8 files
- "Implement registration, catalog, cart, checkout" -> multiple complex features

Skip it:
- "How do I print Hello World in Python?" -> informational
- "Add a comment to calculateTotal" -> single edit
- "Run npm install and tell me what happened" -> one command

When in doubt, use it.

81: ### bodyParser.json([options])
82: 
83: Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
84: the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
85: Unicode encoding of the body.
86: 
87: A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
88: object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).
89: 
90: #### Options
91: 
92: The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
93: the following keys:
94: 
95: ##### defaultCharset
96: 
97: Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
98: specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.
99: 
100: ##### inflate
101: 
102: When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
103: `false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.
104: 
105: ##### limit
106: 
107: Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
108: specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
109: [bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
110: to `'100kb'`.
111: 
112: > It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.
113: 
114: ##### reviver
115: 
116: The `reviver` option is passed directly to `JSON.parse` as the second
117: argument. You can find more information on this argument
118: [in the MDN documentation about JSON.parse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/parse#the_reviver_parameter).
119: 
120: ##### strict
121: 
122: When set to `true`, it will only accept arrays and objects; when `false`, it will
123: accept anything `JSON.parse` accepts. Defaults to `true`.
124: 
125: ##### type
126: 
127: The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
128: parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not a
129: function, `type` option is passed directly to the
130: [type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
131: be an extension name (like `json`), a mime type (like `application/json`), or
132: a mime type with a wildcard (like `*/*` or `*/json`). If a function, the `type`
133: option is called as `fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy
134: value. Defaults to `application/json`.
135: 
136: ##### verify
137: 
138: The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
139: where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the

322: ## Errors
323: 
324: The middlewares provided by this module create errors using the
325: [`http-errors` module](https://www.npmjs.com/package/http-errors). The errors
326: will typically have a `status`/`statusCode` property that contains the suggested
327: HTTP response code, an `expose` property to determine if the `message` property
328: should be displayed to the client, a `type` property to determine the type of
329: error without matching against the `message`, and a `body` property containing
330: the read body, if available.
331: 
332: The following are the common errors created, though any error can come through
333: for various reasons.
334: 
335: ### content encoding unsupported
336: 
337: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
338: contained an encoding but the "inflation" option was set to `false`. The
339: `status` property is set to `415`, the `type` property is set to
340: `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property will be set to the
341: encoding that is unsupported.
342: 
343: ### entity parse failed
344: 
345: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
346: parsed by the middleware. The `status` property is set to `400`, the `type`
347: property is set to `'entity.parse.failed'`, and the `body` property is set to
348: the entity value that failed parsing.
349: 
350: ### entity verify failed
351: 
352: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
353: verified by the defined `verify` option. The `status` property is
354: set to `403`, the `type` property is set to `'entity.verify.failed'`, and the
355: `body` property is set to the entity value that failed verification.
356: 
357: ### request aborted
358: 
359: This error will occur when the request is aborted by the client before reading
360: the body has finished. The `received` property will be set to the number of
361: bytes received before the request was aborted and the `expected` property is
362: set to the number of expected bytes. The `status` property is set to `400`
363: and `type` property is set to `'request.aborted'`.
364: 
365: ### request entity too large
366: 
367: This error will occur when the request body's size is larger than the "limit"
368: option. The `limit` property will be set to the byte limit and the `length`
369: property will be set to the request body's length. The `status` property is
370: set to `413` and the `type` property is set to `'entity.too.large'`.
371: 
372: ### request size did not match content length
373: 
374: This error will occur when the request's length did not match the length from
375: the `Content-Length` header. This typically occurs when the request is malformed,
376: typically when the `Content-Length` header was calculated based on characters
377: instead of bytes. The `status` property is set to `400` and the `type` property
378: is set to `'request.size.invalid'`.
379: 
380: ### stream encoding should not be set
381: 
382: This error will occur when something called the `req.setEncoding` method prior
383: to this middleware. This module operates directly on bytes only and you cannot
384: call `req.setEncoding` when using this module. The `status` property is set to
385: `500` and the `type` property is set to `'stream.encoding.set'`.
386: 
387: ### stream is not readable
388: 
389: This error will occur when the request is no longer readable when this middleware
390: attempts to read it. This typically means something other than a middleware from
391: this module read the request body already and the middleware was also configured to
392: read the same request. The `status` property is set to `500` and the `type`
393: property is set to `'stream.not.readable'`.
394: 
395: ### too many parameters
396: 
397: This error will occur when the content of the request exceeds the configured
398: `parameterLimit` for the `urlencoded` parser. The `status` property is set to
399: `413` and the `type` property is set to `'parameters.too.many'`.
400: 
401: ### unsupported charset "BOGUS"
402: 
403: This error will occur when the request had a charset parameter in the
404: `Content-Type` header, but the `iconv-lite` module does not support it OR the
405: parser does not support it. The charset is contained in the message as well
406: as in the `charset` property. The `status` property is set to `415`, the
407: `type` property is set to `'charset.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property
408: is set to the charset that is unsupported.
409: 
410: ### unsupported content encoding "bogus"
411: 
412: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
413: contained an unsupported encoding. The encoding is contained in the message
414: as well as in the `encoding` property. The `status` property is set to `415`,
415: the `type` property is set to `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `encoding`
416: property is set to the encoding that is unsupported.
417: 
418: ### The input exceeded the depth
419: 
420: This error occurs when using `bodyParser.urlencoded` with the `extended` property set to `true` and the input exceeds the configured `depth` option. The `status` property is set to `400`. ##### rawBody

When set to `true`, the raw request body bytes are made available on
`req.rawBody` as a `Buffer`. The bytes are the decompressed body, after any
`Content-Encoding` (such as `gzip`) has been removed, but before the charset
is decoded, so `req.rawBody` retains the original bytes even when `req.body`
is a decoded object (for example, a `latin1` body keeps its `latin1` bytes).
This is useful for verifying request signatures (such as webhook signatures)
over the exact bytes received. Defaults to `false`, in which case
`req.rawBody` is not set. Works together with the `verify` option, and the
bytes remain available even when body parsing fails.

7. If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first. Use your judgement.

When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.

function.name: todowrite
function.description:
Create and maintain a structured task list for the current coding session. Tracks progress, organizes multi-step work, and surfaces status to the user.

## When to use
Use proactively when:
- The task requires 3+ distinct steps or actions (not just 3 tool calls for a single conceptual step)
- The work is non-trivial and benefits from planning
- The user provides multiple tasks (numbered or comma-separated) or explicitly asks for a todo list
- New instructions arrive - capture them as todos
- You start a task - mark it `in_progress` (only one at a time) before working
- You finish a task - mark it `completed` and add any follow-ups discovered during the work

## When NOT to use
Skip when:
- The work is a single, straightforward task (or <3 trivial steps)
- The request is purely informational or conversational
- Tracking adds no organizational value

## States
- `pending` - not started
- `in_progress` - actively working (exactly ONE at a time)
- `completed` - finished successfully
- `cancelled` - no longer needed

## Rules
- Update status in real time; don't batch completions
- Mark `completed` only after the required work is actually done, including any required verification. Never based on intent.
- Keep exactly one `in_progress` while work remains
- If blocked or partial, keep it `in_progress` and add a follow-up todo describing the blocker
- Preserve user-provided commands verbatim (flags, args, order)
- Items should be specific and actionable; break large work into smaller steps

## Examples

Use it:
- "Add a dark mode toggle and run the tests" -> multi-step feature + explicit verification
- "Rename getCwd -> getCurrentWorkingDirectory across the repo" -> grep reveals 15 occurrences in 8 files
- "Implement registration, catalog, cart, checkout" -> multiple complex features

Skip it:
- "How do I print Hello World in Python?" -> informational
- "Add a comment to calculateTotal" -> single edit
- "Run npm install and tell me what happened" -> one command

When in doubt, use it.

34: /**
35:  * Read a request into a buffer and parse.
36:  *
37:  * @param {Object} req
38:  * @param {Object} res
39:  * @param {Function} next
40:  * @param {Function} parse
41:  * @param {Function} debug
42:  * @param {Object} options
43:  * @private
44:  */
45: function read (req, res, next, parse, debug, options) {
46:   if (onFinished.isFinished(req)) {
47:     debug('body already parsed')
48:     next()
49:     return
50:   }
51: 
52:   if (!('body' in req)) {
53:     req.body = undefined
54:   }
55: 
56:   // skip requests without bodies
57:   if (!hasBody(req)) {
58:     debug('skip empty body')
59:     next()
60:     return
61:   }
62: 
63:   debug('content-type %j', req.headers['content-type'])

65:   // determine if request should be parsed
66:   if (!options.shouldParse(req)) {
67:     debug('skip parsing')
68:     next()
69:     return
70:   }

72:   let encoding = null

76:     // validate charset
77:     if (!!options?.isValidCharset && !options.isValidCharset(encoding)) {
78:       debug('invalid charset')
79:       next(createError(415, 'unsupported charset "' + encoding.toUpperCase() + '"', {
80:         charset: encoding,
81:         type: 'charset.unsupported'
82:       }))
83:       return
84:     }
85:   }
86: 
87:   let length
88:   let stream
89: 
90:   const verify = options.verify
91: 
92:   // assert charset is supported before creating the decompression stream, so an
93:   // unsupported charset cannot leave a decoder piped with no error listener
94:   if (verify && encoding !== null && !iconv.encodingExists(encoding)) {
95:     return next(createError(415, 'unsupported charset "' + encoding.toUpperCase() + '"', {
96:       charset: encoding.toLowerCase(),
97:       type: 'charset.unsupported'
98:     }))
99:   }
100: 
101:   try {
102:     const contentEncoding = (req.headers['content-encoding'] || 'identity').toLowerCase()
103: 
104:     debug('content-encoding "%s"', contentEncoding)
105: 
106:     if (options.inflate === false && contentEncoding !== 'identity') {
107:       throw createError(415, 'content encoding unsupported', {
108:         encoding: contentEncoding,
109:         type: 'encoding.unsupported'
110:       })
111:     }
112: 
113:     // get the content stream
114:     if (contentEncoding === 'identity') {
115:       length = req.headers['content-length']
116:       stream = req
117:     } else {
118:       stream = createDecompressionStream(contentEncoding, debug)
119:       req.pipe(stream)
120:     }

122:     return next(err)
123:   }

125:   // set raw-body options
126:   const rawBodyOptions = {

128:     encoding: verify ? null : encoding,
129:     limit: options.limit
130:   }
131: 
132:   // read body
133:   debug('read body')
134:   getBody(stream, rawBodyOptions, function (error, body) {
135:     if (error) {

138:       if (error.type === 'encoding.unsupported') {
139:         // echo back charset
140:         _error = createError(415, 'unsupported charset "' + encoding.toUpperCase() + '"', {
141:           charset: encoding.toLowerCase(),
142:           type: 'charset.unsupported'
143:         })
144:       } else {
145:         // set status code on error
146:         _error = createError(400, error)
147:       }
148: 
149:       // unpipe from stream and destroy
150:       if (stream !== req) {
151:         req.unpipe()
152:         stream.destroy()
153:       }
154: 
155:       // read off entire request
156:       dump(req, function onfinished () {
157:         next(createError(400, _error))
158:       })
159:       return
160:     }
161: 
162:     // detach and destroy the decompression stream to
163:     // avoid decompression errors on the finished stream
164:     if (stream !== req) {
165:       req.unpipe(stream)
166:       stream.on('error', () => {})
167:       stream.destroy()
168: 
169:       // consume any remaining bytes so the HTTP request can finish
170:       req.resume()
171:     }
172: 
173:     // verify
174:     if (verify) {
175:       try {
176:         debug('verify body')
177:         verify(req, res, body, encoding)
178:       } catch (err) {
179:         next(createError(403, err, {
180:           body,
181:           type: err.type || 'entity.verify.failed'
182:         }))
183:         return
184:       }
185:     }
186: 
187:     // parse
188:     let str = body

190:       debug('parse body')
191:       str = typeof body !== 'string' && encoding !== null

194:       req.body = parse(str, encoding)

81: ### bodyParser.json([options])
82: 
83: Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
84: the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
85: Unicode encoding of the body.
86: 
87: A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
88: object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).
89: 
90: #### Options
91: 
92: The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
93: the following keys:
94: 
95: ##### defaultCharset
96: 
97: Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
98: specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.
99: 
100: ##### inflate
101: 
102: When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
103: `false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.
104: 
105: ##### limit
106: 
107: Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
108: specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
109: [bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
110: to `'100kb'`.
111: 
112: > It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.
113: 
114: ##### reviver
115: 
116: The `reviver` option is passed directly to `JSON.parse` as the second
117: argument. You can find more information on this argument
118: [in the MDN documentation about JSON.parse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/parse#the_reviver_parameter).
119: 
120: ##### strict
121: 
122: When set to `true`, it will only accept arrays and objects; when `false`, it will
123: accept anything `JSON.parse` accepts. Defaults to `true`.
124: 
125: ##### type
126: 
127: The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
128: parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not a
129: function, `type` option is passed directly to the
130: [type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
131: be an extension name (like `json`), a mime type (like `application/json`), or
132: a mime type with a wildcard (like `*/*` or `*/json`). If a function, the `type`
133: option is called as `fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy
134: value. Defaults to `application/json`.
135: 
136: ##### verify
137: 
138: The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
139: where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
140: encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.
141: 
142: ### bodyParser.raw([options])
143: 
144: Returns middleware that parses all bodies as a `Buffer` and only looks at
145: requests where the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option.
146: 
147: A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
148: object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`). This will be a `Buffer` object
149: of the body.
150: 
151: #### Options
152: 
153: The `raw` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
154: the following keys:
155: 
156: ##### inflate
157: 
158: When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
159: `false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.
160: 
161: ##### limit
162: 
163: Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
164: specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
165: [bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
166: to `'100kb'`.
167: 
168: > It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.
169: 
170: ##### type
171: 
172: The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
173: parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function.
174: If not a function, `type` option is passed directly to the
175: [type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this
176: can be an extension name (like `bin`), a mime type (like
177: `application/octet-stream`), or a mime type with a wildcard (like `*/*` or
178: `application/*`). If a function, the `type` option is called as `fn(req)`
179: and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy value. Defaults to
180: `application/octet-stream`.
181: 
182: ##### verify
183: 
184: The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
185: where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
186: encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.
187: 
188: ### bodyParser.text([options])
189: 
190: Returns middleware that parses all bodies as a string and only looks at
191: requests where the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option.
192: 
193: A new `body` string containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
194: object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`). This will be a string of the
195: body.
196: 
197: #### Options
198: 
199: The `text` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
200: the following keys:
201: 
202: ##### defaultCharset
203: 
204: Specify the default character set for the text content if the charset is not
205: specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.
206: 
207: ##### inflate
208: 
209: When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
210: `false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.
211: 
212: ##### limit
213: 
214: Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
215: specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
216: [bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
217: to `'100kb'`.
218: 
219: > It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.
220: 
221: ##### type
222: 
223: The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
224: parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not
225: a function, `type` option is passed directly to the
226: [type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
227: be an extension name (like `txt`), a mime type (like `text/plain`), or a mime
228: type with a wildcard (like `*/*` or `text/*`). If a function, the `type`
229: option is called as `fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a
230: truthy value. Defaults to `text/plain`.
231: 
232: ##### verify
233: 
234: The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
235: where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
236: encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.
237: 
238: ### bodyParser.urlencoded([options])
239: 
240: Returns middleware that only parses `urlencoded` bodies and only looks at
241: requests where the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This
242: parser accepts only UTF-8 and ISO-8859-1 encodings of the body.
243: 
244: A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
245: object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`). This object will contain
246: key-value pairs, where the value can be a string or array (when `extended` is
247: `false`), or any type (when `extended` is `true`).
248: 
249: #### Options
250: 
251: The `urlencoded` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain
252: any of the following keys:
253: 
254: ##### extended
255: 
256: The "extended" syntax allows for rich objects and arrays to be encoded into the
257: URL-encoded format, allowing for a JSON-like experience with URL-encoded. For
258: more information, please [see the qs
259: library](https://www.npmjs.com/package/qs#readme).
260: 
261: Defaults to `false`.
262: 
263: ##### inflate
264: 
265: When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
266: `false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.
267: 
268: ##### limit
269: 
270: Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
271: specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
272: [bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
273: to `'100kb'`.
274: 
275: > It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.
276: 
277: ##### parameterLimit
278: 
279: The `parameterLimit` option controls the maximum number of parameters that
280: are allowed in the URL-encoded data. If a request contains more parameters
281: than this value, a 413 will be returned to the client. Defaults to `1000`.
282: 
283: ##### type
284: 
285: The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
286: parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not
287: a function, `type` option is passed directly to the
288: [type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
289: be an extension name (like `urlencoded`), a mime type (like
290: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`), or a mime type with a wildcard (like
291: `*/x-www-form-urlencoded`). If a function, the `type` option is called as
292: `fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy value. Defaults
293: to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.
294: 
295: ##### verify
296: 
297: The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
298: where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
299: encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.
300: 
301: ##### defaultCharset
302: 
303: The default charset to parse as, if not specified in content-type. Must be
304: either `utf-8` or `iso-8859-1`. Defaults to `utf-8`.
305: 
306: ##### charsetSentinel
307: 
308: Whether to let the value of the `utf8` parameter take precedence as the charset
309: selector. It requires the form to contain a parameter named `utf8` with a value
310: of `✓`. Defaults to `false`.
311: 
312: ##### interpretNumericEntities
313: 
314: Whether to decode numeric entities such as `☺` when parsing an iso-8859-1
315: form. Defaults to `false`.
316: 
317: 
318: ##### depth
319: 
320: The `depth` option is used to configure the maximum depth of the `qs` library when `extended` is `true`. This allows you to limit the amount of keys that are parsed and can be useful to prevent certain types of abuse. Defaults to `32`. It is recommended to keep this value as low as possible.
321: 
322: ## Errors
323: 
324: The middlewares provided by this module create errors using the
325: [`http-errors` module](https://www.npmjs.com/package/http-errors). The errors
326: will typically have a `status`/`statusCode` property that contains the suggested
327: HTTP response code, an `expose` property to determine if the `message` property
328: should be displayed to the client, a `type` property to determine the type of
329: error without matching against the `message`, and a `body` property containing
330: the read body, if available.
331: 
332: The following are the common errors created, though any error can come through
333: for various reasons.
334: 
335: ### content encoding unsupported
336: 
337: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
338: contained an encoding but the "inflation" option was set to `false`. The
339: `status` property is set to `415`, the `type` property is set to
340: `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property will be set to the
341: encoding that is unsupported.
342: 
343: ### entity parse failed
344: 
345: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
346: parsed by the middleware. The `status` property is set to `400`, the `type`
347: property is set to `'entity.parse.failed'`, and the `body` property is set to
348: the entity value that failed parsing.
349: 
350: ### entity verify failed
351: 
352: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
353: verified by the defined `verify` option. The `status` property is
354: set to `403`, the `type` property is set to `'entity.verify.failed'`, and the
355: `body` property is set to the entity value that failed verification.
356: 
357: ### request aborted
358: 
359: This error will occur when the request is aborted by the client before reading
360: the body has finished. The `received` property will be set to the number of
361: bytes received before the request was aborted and the `expected` property is
362: set to the number of expected bytes. The `status` property is set to `400`
363: and `type` property is set to `'request.aborted'`.
364: 
365: ### request entity too large
366: 
367: This error will occur when the request body's size is larger than the "limit"
368: option. The `limit` property will be set to the byte limit and the `length`
369: property will be set to the request body's length. The `status` property is
370: set to `413` and the `type` property is set to `'entity.too.large'`.
371: 
372: ### request size did not match content length
373: 
374: This error will occur when the request's length did not match the length from
375: the `Content-Length` header. This typically occurs when the request is malformed,
376: typically when the `Content-Length` header was calculated based on characters
377: instead of bytes. The `status` property is set to `400` and the `type` property
378: is set to `'request.size.invalid'`.
379: 
380: ### stream encoding should not be set
381: 
382: This error will occur when something called the `req.setEncoding` method prior
383: to this middleware. This module operates directly on bytes only and you cannot
384: call `req.setEncoding` when using this module. The `status` property is set to
385: `500` and the `type` property is set to `'stream.encoding.set'`.
386: 
387: ### stream is not readable
388: 
389: This error will occur when the request is no longer readable when this middleware
390: attempts to read it. This typically means something other than a middleware from
391: this module read the request body already and the middleware was also configured to
392: read the same request. The `status` property is set to `500` and the `type`
393: property is set to `'stream.not.readable'`.
394: 
395: ### too many parameters
396: 
397: This error will occur when the content of the request exceeds the configured
398: `parameterLimit` for the `urlencoded` parser. The `status` property is set to
399: `413` and the `type` property is set to `'parameters.too.many'`.
400: 
401: ### unsupported charset "BOGUS"
402: 
403: This error will occur when the request had a charset parameter in the
404: `Content-Type` header, but the `iconv-lite` module does not support it OR the
405: parser does not support it. The charset is contained in the message as well
406: as in the `charset` property. The `status` property is set to `415`, the
407: `type` property is set to `'charset.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property
408: is set to the charset that is unsupported.
409: 
410: ### unsupported content encoding "bogus"
411: 
412: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
413: contained an unsupported encoding. The encoding is contained in the message
414: as well as in the `encoding` property. The `status` property is set to `415`,
415: the `type` property is set to `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `encoding`
416: property is set to the encoding that is unsupported.
417: 
418: ### The input exceeded the depth
419: 
420: This error occurs when using `bodyParser.urlencoded` with the `extended` property set to `true` and the input exceeds the configured `depth` option. The `status` property is set to `400`. It is recommended to review the `depth` option and evaluate if it requires a higher value. With the default `depth` of `32`, an input with 33 or more levels of nesting gets this error.

function.name: todowrite
function.description:
Create and maintain a structured task list for the current coding session. Tracks progress, organizes multi-step work, and surfaces status to the user.

## When to use
Use proactively when:
- The task requires 3+ distinct steps or actions (not just 3 tool calls for a single conceptual step)
- The work is non-trivial and benefits from planning
- The user provides multiple tasks (numbered or comma-separated) or explicitly asks for a todo list
- New instructions arrive - capture them as todos
- You start a task - mark it `in_progress` (only one at a time) before working
- You finish a task - mark it `completed` and add any follow-ups discovered during the work

## When NOT to use
Skip when:
- The work is a single, straightforward task (or <3 trivial steps)
- The request is purely informational or conversational
- Tracking adds no organizational value

## States
- `pending` - not started
- `in_progress` - actively working (exactly ONE at a time)
- `completed` - finished successfully
- `cancelled` - no longer needed

## Rules
- Update status in real time; don't batch completions
- Mark `completed` only after the required work is actually done, including any required verification. Never based on intent.
- Keep exactly one `in_progress` while work remains
- If blocked or partial, keep it `in_progress` and add a follow-up todo describing the blocker
- Preserve user-provided commands verbatim (flags, args, order)
- Items should be specific and actionable; break large work into smaller steps

## Examples

Use it:
- "Add a dark mode toggle and run the tests" -> multi-step feature + explicit verification
- "Rename getCwd -> getCurrentWorkingDirectory across the repo" -> grep reveals 15 occurrences in 8 files
- "Implement registration, catalog, cart, checkout" -> multiple complex features

Skip it:
- "How do I print Hello World in Python?" -> informational
- "Add a comment to calculateTotal" -> single edit
- "Run npm install and tell me what happened" -> one command

When in doubt, use it.

81: ### bodyParser.json([options])
82: 
83: Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
84: the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
85: Unicode encoding of the body.
86: 
87: A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
88: object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).
89: 
90: #### Options
91: 
92: The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
93: the following keys:
94: 
95: ##### defaultCharset
96: 
97: Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
98: specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.
99: 
100: ##### inflate
101: 
102: When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
103: `false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.
104: 
105: ##### limit
106: 
107: Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
108: specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
109: [bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
110: to `'100kb'`.
111: 
112: > It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.
113: 
114: ##### reviver
115: 
116: The `reviver` option is passed directly to `JSON.parse` as the second
117: argument. You can find more information on this argument
118: [in the MDN documentation about JSON.parse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/parse#the_reviver_parameter).
119: 
120: ##### strict
121: 
122: When set to `true`, it will only accept arrays and objects; when `false`, it will
123: accept anything `JSON.parse` accepts. Defaults to `true`.
124: 
125: ##### type
126: 
127: The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
128: parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not a
129: function, `type` option is passed directly to the
130: [type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
131: be an extension name (like `json`), a mime type (like `application/json`), or
132: a mime type with a wildcard (like `*/*` or `*/json`). If a function, the `type`
133: option is called as `fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy
134: value. Defaults to `application/json`.
135: 
136: ##### verify

138: The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
139: where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
140: encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.

297: The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
298: where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
299: encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.
300: 
301: ##### defaultCharset
302: 
303: The default charset to parse as, if not specified in content-type. Must be
304: either `utf-8` or `iso-8859-1`. Defaults to `utf-8`.
305: 
306: ##### charsetSentinel
307: 
308: Whether to let the value of the `utf8` parameter take precedence as the charset
309: selector. It requires the form to contain a parameter named `utf8` with a value
310: of `✓`. Defaults to `false`.
311: 
312: ##### interpretNumericEntities
313: 
314: Whether to decode numeric entities such as `☺` when parsing an iso-8859-1
315: form. Defaults to `false`.
316: 
317: 
318: ##### depth
319: 
320: The `depth` option is used to configure the maximum depth of the `qs` library when `extended` is `true`. This allows you to limit the amount of keys that are parsed and can be useful to prevent certain types of abuse. Defaults to `32`. It is recommended to keep this value as low as possible.
321: 
322: ## Errors
323: 
324: The middlewares provided by this module create errors using the
325: [`http-errors` module](https://www.npmjs.com/package/http-errors). The errors
326: will typically have a `status`/`statusCode` property that contains the suggested
327: HTTP response code, an `expose` property to determine if the `message` property
328: should be displayed to the client, a `type` property to determine the type of
329: error without matching against the `message`, and a `body` property containing
330: the read body, if available.
331: 
332: The following are the common errors created, though any error can come through
333: for various reasons.
334: 
335: ### content encoding unsupported
336: 
337: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
338: contained an encoding but the "inflation" option was set to `false`. The
339: `status` property is set to `415`, the `type` property is set to
340: `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property will be set to the
341: encoding that is unsupported.
342: 
343: ### entity parse failed
344: 
345: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
346: parsed by the middleware. The `status` property is set to `400`, the `type`
347: property is set to `'entity.parse.failed'`, and the `body` property is set to
348: the entity value that failed parsing.
349: 
350: ### entity verify failed
351: 
352: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
353: verified by the defined `verify` option. The `status` property is
354: set to `403`, the `type` property is set to `'entity.verify.failed'`, and the
355: `body` property is set to the entity value that failed verification.
356: 
357: ### request aborted
358: 
359: This error will occur when the request is aborted by the client before reading
360: the body has finished. The `received` property will be set to the number of
361: bytes received before the request was aborted and the `expected` property is
362: set to the number of expected bytes. The `status` property is set to `400`
363: and `type` property is set to `'request.aborted'`.
364: 
365: ### request entity too large
366: 
367: This error will occur when the request body's size is larger than the "limit"
368: option. The `limit` property will be set to the byte limit and the `length`
369: property will be set to the request body's length. The `status` property is
370: set to `413` and the `type` property is set to `'entity.too.large'`.
371: 
372: ### request size did not match content length
373: 
374: This error will occur when the request's length did not match the length from
375: the `Content-Length` header. This typically occurs when the request is malformed,
376: typically when the `Content-Length` header was calculated based on characters
377: instead of bytes. The `status` property is set to `400` and the `type` property
378: is set to `'request.size.invalid'`.
379: 
380: ### stream encoding should not be set
381: 
382: This error will occur when something called the `req.setEncoding` method prior
383: to this middleware. This module operates directly on bytes only and you cannot
384: call `req.setEncoding` when using this module. The `status` property is set to
385: `500` and the `type` property is set to `'stream.encoding.set'`.
386: 
387: ### stream is not readable
388: 
389: This error will occur when the request is no longer readable when this middleware
390: attempts to read it. This typically means something other than a middleware from
391: this module read the request body already and the middleware was also configured to
392: read the same request. The `status` property is set to `500` and the `type`
393: property is set to `'stream.not.readable'`.
394: 
395: ### too many parameters
396: 
397: This error will occur when the content of the request exceeds the configured
398: `parameterLimit` for the `urlencoded` parser. The `status` property is set to
399: `413` and the `type` property is set to `'parameters.too.many'`.
400: 
401: ### unsupported charset "BOGUS"
402: 
403: This error will occur when the request had a charset parameter in the
404: `Content-Type` header, but the `iconv-lite` module does not support it OR the
405: parser does not support it. The charset is contained in the message as well
406: as in the `charset` property. The `status` property is set to `415`, the
407: `type` property is set to `'charset.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property
408: is set to the charset that is unsupported.
409: 
410: ### unsupported content encoding "bogus"
411: 
412: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
413: contained an unsupported encoding. The encoding is contained in the message
414: as well as in the `encoding` property. The `status` property is set to `415`,
415: the `type` property is set to `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `encoding`
416: property is set to the encoding that is unsupported.
417: 
418: ### The input exceeded the depth
419: 
420: This error occurs when using `bodyParser.urlencoded` with the `extended` property set to `true` and the input exceeds the configured `depth` option. The `status` property is set to `400`. It is recommended to review the `depth` option and evaluate if it requires a higher value. With the default `depth` of `32`, an input with 33 or more levels of nesting gets this error.

function.name: todowrite
function.description:
Create and maintain a structured task list for the current coding session. Tracks progress, organizes multi-step work, and surfaces status to the user.

## When to use
Use proactively when:
- The task requires 3+ distinct steps or actions (not just 3 tool calls for a single conceptual step)
- The work is non-trivial and benefits from planning
- The user provides multiple tasks (numbered or comma-separated) or explicitly asks for a todo list
- New instructions arrive - capture them as todos
- You start a task - mark it `in_progress` (only one at a time) before working
- You finish a task - mark it `completed` and add any follow-ups discovered during the work

## When NOT to use
Skip when:
- The work is a single, straightforward task (or <3 trivial steps)
- The request is purely informational or conversational
- Tracking adds no organizational value

## States
- `pending` - not started
- `in_progress` - actively working (exactly ONE at a time)
- `completed` - finished successfully
- `cancelled` - no longer needed

## Rules
- Update status in real time; don't batch completions
- Mark `completed` only after the required work is actually done, including any required verification. Never based on intent.
- Keep exactly one `in_progress` while work remains
- If blocked or partial, keep it `in_progress` and add a follow-up todo describing the blocker
- Preserve user-provided commands verbatim (flags, args, order)
- Items should be specific and actionable; break large work into smaller steps

## Examples

Use it:
- "Add a dark mode toggle and run the tests" -> multi-step feature + explicit verification
- "Rename getCwd -> getCurrentWorkingDirectory across the repo" -> grep reveals 15 occurrences in 8 files
- "Implement registration, catalog, cart, checkout" -> multiple complex features

Skip it:
- "How do I print Hello World in Python?" -> informational
- "Add a comment to calculateTotal" -> single edit
- "Run npm install and tell me what happened" -> one command

When in doubt, use it.

81: ### bodyParser.json([options])
82: 
83: Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
84: the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
85: Unicode encoding of the body.
86: 
87: A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
88: object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).
89: 
90: #### Options
91: 
92: The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
93: the following keys:
94: 
95: ##### defaultCharset
96: 
97: Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
98: specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.
99: 
100: ##### inflate
101: 
102: When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
103: `false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.
104: 
105: ##### limit
106: 
107: Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
108: specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
109: [bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
110: to `'100kb'`.
111: 
112: > It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.
113: 
114: ##### reviver
115: 
116: The `reviver` option is passed directly to `JSON.parse` as the second
117: argument. You can find more information on this argument
118: [in the MDN documentation about JSON.parse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/parse#the_reviver_parameter).
119: 
120: ##### strict
121: 
122: When set to `true`, it will only accept arrays and objects; when `false`, it will
123: accept anything `JSON.parse` accepts. Defaults to `true`.

134: value. Defaults to `application/json`.

238: ### bodyParser.urlencoded([options])
239: 
240: Returns middleware that only parses `urlencoded` bodies and only looks at
241: requests where the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This
242: parser accepts only UTF-8 and ISO-8859-1 encodings of the body.

248: 
249: #### Options
250: 
251: The `urlencoded` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain
252: any of the following keys:
253: 
254: ##### extended
255: 
256: The "extended" syntax allows for rich objects and arrays to be encoded into the
257: URL-encoded format, allowing for a JSON-like experience with URL-encoded. For
258: more information, please [see the qs
259: library](https://www.npmjs.com/package/qs#readme).

261: Defaults to `false`.

Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. 289: be an extension name (like `urlencoded`), a mime type (like

291: `*/x-www-form-urlencoded`). If a function, the `type` option is called as
292: `fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy value. Defaults
293: to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

304: either `utf-8` or `iso-8859-1`. Defaults to `utf-8`.
305: 
306: ##### charsetSentinel
307: 
308: Whether to let the value of the `utf8` parameter take precedence as the charset
309: selector. It requires the form to contain a parameter named `utf8` with a value
310: of `✓`. Defaults to `false`.
311: 
312: ##### interpretNumericEntities
313: 
314: Whether to decode numeric entities such as `☺` when parsing an iso-8859-1
315: form. Defaults to `false`.
316: 
317: 
318: ##### depth
319: 
320: The `depth` option is used to configure the maximum depth of the `qs` library when `extended` is `true`. This allows you to limit the amount of keys that are parsed and can be useful to prevent certain types of abuse. Defaults to `32`. It is recommended to keep this value as low as possible.
321: 
322: ## Errors
323: 
324: The middlewares provided by this module create errors using the
325: [`http-errors` module](https://www.npmjs.com/package/http-errors). The errors
326: will typically have a `status`/`statusCode` property that contains the suggested
327: HTTP response code, an `expose` property to determine if the `message` property
328: should be displayed to the client, a `type` property to determine the type of
329: error without matching against the `message`, and a `body` property containing
330: the read body, if available.
331: 
332: The following are the common errors created, though any error can come through
333: for various reasons.
334: 
335: ### content encoding unsupported
336: 
337: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
338: contained an encoding but the "inflation" option was set to `false`. The
339: `status` property is set to `415`, the `type` property is set to
340: `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property will be set to the
341: encoding that is unsupported.
342: 
343: ### entity parse failed
344: 
345: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
346: parsed by the middleware. The `status` property is set to `400`, the `type`
347: property is set to `'entity.parse.failed'`, and the `body` property is set to
348: the entity value that failed parsing.
349: 
350: ### entity verify failed
351: 
352: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
353: verified by the defined `verify` option. The `status` property is
354: set to `403`, the `type` property is set to `'entity.verify.failed'`, and the
355: `body` property is set to the entity value that failed verification.
356: 
357: ### request aborted
358: 
359: This error will occur when the request is aborted by the client before reading
360: the body has finished. The `received` property will be set to the number of
361: bytes received before the request was aborted and the `expected` property is
362: set to the number of expected bytes. The `status` property is set to `400`
363: and `type` property is set to `'request.aborted'`.
364: 
365: ### request entity too large
366: 
367: This error will occur when the request body's size is larger than the "limit"
368: option. The `limit` property will be set to the byte limit and the `length`
369: property will be set to the request body's length. The `status` property is
370: set to `413` and the `type` property is set to `'entity.too.large'`.
371: 
372: ### request size did not match content length
373: 
374: This error will occur when the request's length did not match the length from
375: the `Content-Length` header. This typically occurs when the request is malformed,
376: typically when the `Content-Length` header was calculated based on characters
377: instead of bytes. The `status` property is set to `400` and the `type` property
378: is set to `'request.size.invalid'`.
379: 
380: ### stream encoding should not be set
381: 
382: This error will occur when something called the `req.setEncoding` method prior
383: to this middleware. This module operates directly on bytes only and you cannot
384: call `req.setEncoding` when using this module. The `status` property is set to
385: `500` and the `type` property is set to `'stream.encoding.set'`.
386: 
387: ### stream is not readable
388: 
389: This error will occur when the request is no longer readable when this middleware
390: attempts to read it. This typically means something other than a middleware from
391: this module read the request body already and the middleware was also configured to
392: read the same request. The `status` property is set to `500` and the `type`
393: property is set to `'stream.not.readable'`.
394: 
395: ### too many parameters
396: 
397: This error will occur when the content of the request exceeds the configured
398: `parameterLimit` for the `urlencoded` parser. The `status` property is set to
399: `413` and the `type` property is set to `'parameters.too.many'`.
400: 
401: ### unsupported charset "BOGUS"
402: 
403: This error will occur when the request had a charset parameter in the
404: `Content-Type` header, but the `iconv-lite` module does not support it OR the
405: parser does not support it. The charset is contained in the message as well
406: as in the `charset` property. The `status` property is set to `415`, the
407: `type` property is set to `'charset.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property
408: is set to the charset that is unsupported.
409: 
410: ### unsupported content encoding "bogus"
411: 
412: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
413: contained an unsupported encoding. The encoding is contained in the message
414: as well as in the `encoding` property. The `status` property is set to `415`,
415: the `type` property is set to `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `encoding`
416: property is set to the encoding that is unsupported.
417: 
418: ### The input exceeded the depth
419: 
420: This error occurs when using `bodyParser.urlencoded` with the `extended` property set to `true` and the input exceeds the configured `depth` option. The `status` property is set to `400`. It is recommended to review the `depth` option and evaluate if it requires a higher value. With the default `depth` of `32`, an input with 33 or more levels of nesting gets this error.

function.name: todowrite
function.description:
Create and maintain a structured task list for the current coding session. Tracks progress, organizes multi-step work, and surfaces status to the user.

## When to use
Use proactively when:
- The task requires 3+ distinct steps or actions (not just 3 tool calls for a single conceptual step)
- The work is non-trivial and benefits from planning
- The user provides multiple tasks (numbered or comma-separated) or explicitly asks for a todo list
- New instructions arrive - capture them as todos
- You start a task - mark it `in_progress` (only one at a time) before working
- You finish a task - mark it `completed` and add any follow-ups discovered during the work

## When NOT to use
Skip when:
- The work is a single, straightforward task (or <3 trivial steps)
- The request is purely informational or conversational
- Tracking adds no organizational value

## States
- `pending` - not started
- `in_progress` - actively working (exactly ONE at a time)
- `completed` - finished successfully
- `cancelled` - no longer needed

## Rules
- Update status in real time; don't batch completions
- Mark `completed` only after the required work is actually done, including any required verification. Never based on intent.
- Keep exactly one `in_progress` while work remains
- If blocked or partial, keep it `in_progress` and add a follow-up todo describing the blocker
- Preserve user-provided commands verbatim (flags, args, order)
- Items should be specific and actionable; break large work into smaller steps

## Examples

Use it:
- "Add a dark mode toggle and run the tests" -> multi-step feature + explicit verification
- "Rename getCwd -> getCurrentWorkingDirectory across the repo" -> grep reveals 15 occurrences in 8 files
- "Implement registration, catalog, cart, checkout" -> multiple complex features

Skip it:
- "How do I print Hello World in Python?" -> informational
- "Add a comment to calculateTotal" -> single edit
- "Run npm install and tell me what happened" -> one command

When in doubt, use it.
