322: ## Errors
323: 
324: The middlewares provided by this module create errors using the
325: [`http-errors` module](https://www.npmjs.com/package/http-errors). The errors
326: will typically have a `status`/`statusCode` property that contains the suggested
327: HTTP response code, an `expose` property to determine if the `message` property
328: should be displayed to the client, a `type` property to determine the type of
329: error without matching against the `message`, and a `body` property containing
330: the read body, if available.
331: 
332: The following are the common errors created, though any error can come through
333: for various reasons.
334: 
335: ### content encoding unsupported
336: 
337: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
338: contained an encoding but the "inflation" option was set to `false`. The
339: `status` property is set to `415`, the `type` property is set to
340: `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property will be set to the
341: encoding that is unsupported.
342: 
343: ### entity parse failed
344: 
345: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
346: parsed by the middleware. The `status` property is set to `400`, the `type`
347: property is set to `'entity.parse.failed'`, and the `body` property is set to
348: the entity value that failed parsing.
349: 
350: ### entity verify failed
351: 
352: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
353: verified by the defined `verify` option. The `status` property is
354: set to `403`, the `type` property is set to `'entity.verify.failed'`, and the
355: `body` property is set to the entity value that failed verification.
356: 
357: ### request aborted
358: 
359: This error will occur when the request is aborted by the client before reading
360: the body has finished. The `received` property will be set to the number of
361: bytes received before the request was aborted and the `expected` property is
362: set to the number of expected bytes. The `status` property is set to `400`
363: and `type` property is set to `'request.aborted'`.
364: 
365: ### request entity too large
366: 
367: This error will occur when the request body's size is larger than the "limit"
368: option. The `limit` property will be set to the byte limit and the `length`
369: property will be set to the request body's length. The `status` property is
370: set to `413` and the `type` property is set to `'entity.too.large'`.
371: 
372: ### request size did not match content length
373: 
374: This error will occur when the request's length did not match the length from
375: the `Content-Length` header. This typically occurs when the request is malformed,
376: typically when the `Content-Length` header was calculated based on characters
377: instead of bytes. The `status` property is set to `400` and the `type` property
378: is set to `'request.size.invalid'`.
379: 
380: ### stream encoding should not be set
381: 
382: This error will occur when something called the `req.setEncoding` method prior
383: to this middleware. This module operates directly on bytes only and you cannot
384: call `req.setEncoding` when using this module. The `status` property is set to
385: `500` and the `type` property is set to `'stream.encoding.set'`.
386: 
387: ### stream is not readable
388: 
389: This error will occur when the request is no longer readable when this middleware
390: attempts to read it. This typically means something other than a middleware from
391: this module read the request body already and the middleware was also configured to
392: read the same request. The `status` property is set to `500` and the `type`
393: property is set to `'stream.not.readable'`.
394: 
395: ### too many parameters
396: 
397: This error will occur when the content of the request exceeds the configured
398: `parameterLimit` for the `urlencoded` parser. The `status` property is set to
399: `413` and the `type` property is set to `'parameters.too.many'`.
400: 
401: ### unsupported charset "BOGUS"
402: 
403: This error will occur when the request had a charset parameter in the
404: `Content-Type` header, but the `iconv-lite` module does not support it OR the
405: parser does not support it. The charset is contained in the message as well
406: as in the `charset` property. The `status` property is set to `415`, the
407: `type` property is set to `'charset.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property
408: is set to the charset that is unsupported.
409: 
410: ### unsupported content encoding "bogus"
411: 
412: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
413: contained an unsupported encoding. The encoding is contained in the message
414: as well as in the `encoding` property. The `status` property is set to `415`,
415: the `type` property is set to `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `encoding`
416: property is set to the encoding that is unsupported.
417: 
418: ### The input exceeded the depth
419: 
420: This error occurs when using `bodyParser.urlencoded` with the `extended` property set to `true` and the input exceeds the configured `depth` option. The `status` property is set to `400`. It is recommended to review the `depth` option and evaluate if it requires a higher value. With the default `depth` of `32`, an input with 33 or more levels of nesting gets this error.

Use proactively when:

Skip when:

- `pending` - not started

- `completed` - finished successfully
- `cancelled` - no longer needed

- Update status in real time; don't batch completions
- Mark `completed` only after the required work is actually done, including any required verification. Never based on intent.

81: ### bodyParser.json([options])
82: 
83: Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
84: the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
85: Unicode encoding of the body.
86: 
87: A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
88: object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).
89: 
90: #### Options
91: 
92: The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
93: the following keys:
94: 
95: ##### defaultCharset
96: 
97: Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
98: specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.
99: 
100: ##### inflate
101: 
102: When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
103: `false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.
104: 
105: ##### limit
106: 
107: Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
108: specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
109: [bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
110: to `'100kb'`.
111: 
112: > It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.
113: 
114: ##### reviver
115: 
116: The `reviver` option is passed directly to `JSON.parse` as the second
117: argument. You can find more information on this argument
118: [in the MDN documentation about JSON.parse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/parse#the_reviver_parameter).
119: 
120: ##### strict
121: 
122: When set to `true`, it will only accept arrays and objects; when `false`, it will
123: accept anything `JSON.parse` accepts. Defaults to `true`.
124: 
125: ##### type
126: 
127: The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
128: parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not a
129: function, `type` option is passed directly to the
130: [type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
131: be an extension name (like `json`), a mime type (like `application/json`), or
132: a mime type with a wildcard (like `*/*` or `*/json`). If a function, the `type`
133: option is called as `fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy
134: value. Defaults to `application/json`.
135: 
136: ##### verify
137: 
138: The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
139: where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
140: encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.
141: 
142: ### bodyParser.raw([options])
143: 
144: Returns middleware that parses all bodies as a `Buffer` and only looks at
145: requests where the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option.
146: 
147: A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
148: object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`). This will be a `Buffer` object
149: of the body.
150: 
151: #### Options
152: 
153: The `raw` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
154: the following keys:
155: 
156: ##### inflate
157: 
158: When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
159: `false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.
160: 
161: ##### limit
162: 
163: Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
164: specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
165: [bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults

322: ## Errors
323: 
324: The middlewares provided by this module create errors using the
325: [`http-errors` module](https://www.npmjs.com/package/http-errors). The errors

328: should be displayed to the client, a `type` property to determine the type of
329: error without matching against the `message`, and a `body` property containing
330: the read body, if available.

333: for various reasons.
334: 
335: ### content encoding unsupported
336: 
337: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
338: contained an encoding but the "inflation" option was set to `false`. The
339: `status` property is set to `415`, the `type` property is set to
340: `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property will be set to the
341: encoding that is unsupported.
342: 
343: ### entity parse failed
344: 
345: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
346: parsed by the middleware. The `status` property is set to `400`, the `type`
347: property is set to `'entity.parse.failed'`, and the `body` property is set to
348: the entity value that failed parsing.
349: 
350: ### entity verify failed
351: 
352: This error will occur when the request contained an entity that could not be
353: verified by the defined `verify` option. The `status` property is
354: set to `403`, the `type` property is set to `'entity.verify.failed'`, and the
355: `body` property is set to the entity value that failed verification.
356: 
357: ### request aborted
358: 
359: This error will occur when the request is aborted by the client before reading
360: the body has finished. The `received` property will be set to the number of
361: bytes received before the request was aborted and the `expected` property is
362: set to the number of expected bytes. The `status` property is set to `400`
363: and `type` property is set to `'request.aborted'`.
364: 
365: ### request entity too large
366: 
367: This error will occur when the request body's size is larger than the "limit"
368: option. The `limit` property will be set to the byte limit and the `length`
369: property will be set to the request body's length. The `status` property is
370: set to `413` and the `type` property is set to `'entity.too.large'`.
371: 
372: ### request size did not match content length
373: 
374: This error will occur when the request's length did not match the length from
375: the `Content-Length` header. This typically occurs when the request is malformed,
376: typically when the `Content-Length` header was calculated based on characters
377: instead of bytes. The `status` property is set to `400` and the `type` property
378: is set to `'request.size.invalid'`.
379: 
380: ### stream encoding should not be set
381: 
382: This error will occur when something called the `req.setEncoding` method prior
383: to this middleware. This module operates directly on bytes only and you cannot
384: call `req.setEncoding` when using this module. The `status` property is set to
385: `500` and the `type` property is set to `'stream.encoding.set'`.
386: 
387: ### stream is not readable
388: 
389: This error will occur when the request is no longer readable when this middleware
390: attempts to read it. This typically means something other than a middleware from
391: this module read the request body already and the middleware was also configured to
392: read the same request. The `status` property is set to `500` and the `type`
393: property is set to `'stream.not.readable'`.
394: 
395: ### too many parameters
396: 
397: This error will occur when the content of the request exceeds the configured
398: `parameterLimit` for the `urlencoded` parser. The `status` property is set to
399: `413` and the `type` property is set to `'parameters.too.many'`.
400: 
401: ### unsupported charset "BOGUS"
402: 
403: This error will occur when the request had a charset parameter in the
404: `Content-Type` header, but the `iconv-lite` module does not support it OR the
405: parser does not support it. The charset is contained in the message as well
406: as in the `charset` property. The `status` property is set to `415`, the
407: `type` property is set to `'charset.unsupported'`, and the `charset` property
408: is set to the charset that is unsupported.
409: 
410: ### unsupported content encoding "bogus"
411: 
412: This error will occur when the request had a `Content-Encoding` header that
413: contained an unsupported encoding. The encoding is contained in the message
414: as well as in the `encoding` property. The `status` property is set to `415`,
415: the `type` property is set to `'encoding.unsupported'`, and the `encoding`
416: property is set to the encoding that is unsupported.
417: 
418: ### The input exceeded the depth
419: 
420: This error occurs when using `bodyParser.urlencoded` with the `extended` property set to `true` and the input exceeds the configured `depth` option. The `status` property is set to `400`. Use proactively when:

- The work is non-trivial and benefits from planning

- "How do I print Hello World in Python?" -> informational
- "Add a comment to calculateTotal" -> single edit

message.content:
Implemented the `rawBody` option across all four parsers.

**Core changes:**
- `lib/utils.js`: `normalizeOptions` now exposes `rawBody` (strictly `=== true`).
- `lib/read.js:94,132,178`:
  - Reads the body as a `Buffer` (`encoding: null`) whenever `rawBody` is true, so bytes are captured after `Content-Encoding` decompression but before charset decoding.
  - Sets `req.rawBody = body` right after a successful read and before `verify`/parse, so bytes persist even when verification or parsing fails.
  - Extended the charset-support pre-check to `(verify || rawBody)` to preserve the existing 415 behavior.

**Behavior:**
- `rawBody: true` → `req.rawBody` is a `Buffer` with decompressed, pre-charset-decode bytes (e.g. latin1 body keeps latin1 bytes while `req.body` is decoded).
- Missing/`false`/any other value → `req.rawBody` is not set.
- Works alongside `verify`, and bytes survive parse failures.

**Docs/Tests:**
- Documented `rawBody` in all four parser option sections in `README.md`.
- Added tests in `test/{json,raw,text,urlencoded}.js` and `test/utils.js` covering default absence, truthiness, latin1/iso-8859-1 bytes, gzip decompression, parse/verify failures, and `verify` interplay.

`npm test` → 301 passing, `npm run lint` clean.

```js
// Import all parsers
const bodyParser = require('body-parser')

// Or import individual parsers directly
const json = require('body-parser/json')
const urlencoded = require('body-parser/urlencoded')
const raw = require('body-parser/raw')
const text = require('body-parser/text')
```

The `bodyParser` object exposes various factories to create middlewares. All

- "aur body parse fail hone par bhi bytes wahin rehne chahiye." and on body parse failure, the bytes should remain there.

The parsers pass `normalizedOptions` to read via readOptions (spread). So adding `rawBody` in normalizeOptions makes it available. ...

But wait, "Content-Encoding hatne ke baad" — after removing content encoding. raw-body reads from `stream` which is the decompression stream. So body is decompressed bytes. Good.

Now consider the body parse fail case: parse throws. `req.rawBody` already set. Good. Verify throw case: req.rawBody already set (if rawBody true). Good.

Now, there's a nuance: When rawBody is true and `encoding` is null (raw parser), `str = typeof body !== 'string' && encoding !== null ? ... : body` -> body Buffer. parse passthrough. req.body = Buffer. But note: `req.body` and `req.rawBody` would be the same Buffer object. Is that a concern? Probably fine. Actually maybe raw parser already sets req.body to Buffer. rawBody should also be Buffer. Same object is fine.

Hmm, wait. Actually for `raw` parser, `skipCharset: true`, so encoding stays null. Good.

Now, another subtlety: Existing `verify` behavior with rawBody. Let's trace with both verify and rawBody true:
- iconv check (now includes rawBody): if encoding not exists -> 415 before read. Same as verify path already.
- raw-body returns Buffer.
- set req.rawBody = body.
- verify(req,res,body,encoding) - works.
- decode body to str for parse.

Now what about `rawBody` true with an invalid charset like `application/json; charset=bogus`? Previously without verify and without rawBody, raw-body would error with encoding.unsupported -> 415 unsupported charset. With rawBody, we now assert iconv.encodingExists(encoding) and return the same 415. Message would be `unsupported charset "BOGUS"` with charset lowercased. Let's verify existing behavior for json invalid charset test to ensure message matches. Let me check tests.

{

  "output_head": "## API

```js
// Import all parsers
const bodyParser = require('body-parser')

// Or import individual parsers directly
const json = require('body-parser/json')
const urlencoded = require('body-parser/urlencoded')
const raw = require('body-parser/raw')
const text = require('body-parser/text')
```

The `bodyParser` object exposes various factories to create middlewares. All
middlewares will populate the `req.body` property with the parsed body when
the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

**Note** As of v2, `req.body` is left `undefined` when no body is parsed (for
example when the request has neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding`,
or when `Content-Type` does not match). In v1, `req.body` was always initialized
to `{}`. Code that assumes `req.body` is always an object should use optional
chaining (for example `req.body?.username`) or set a default.

The various errors returned by this module are described in the
[errors section](#errors).

### bodyParser.json([options])

Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
Unicode encoding of the body.

A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).

#### Options

The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
the following keys:

##### defaultCharset

Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.

##### inflate

When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
`false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.

##### limit

Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
[bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
to `'100kb'`.

> It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.

##### reviver

The `reviver` option is passed directly to `JSON.parse` as the second
argument. You can find more information on this argument
[in the MDN documentation about JSON.parse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/parse#the_reviver_parameter).

##### strict

When set to `true`, it will only accept arrays and objects; when `false`, it will
accept anything `JSON.parse` accepts. Defaults to `true`.

##### type

The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not a
function, `type` option is passed directly to the
[type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
be an extension name (like `json`), a mime type (like `application/json`), or
a mime type with a wildcard (like `*/*` or `*/json`). If a function, the `type`
option is called as `fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy
value. Defaults to `application/json`.

##### verify

The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.

### bodyParser.raw([options])

Returns middleware that parses all bodies as a `Buffer` and only looks at

// Or import individual parsers directly

The `bodyParser` object exposes various factories to create middlewares. All
middlewares will populate the `req.body` property with the parsed body when
the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

**Note** As of v2, `req.body` is left `undefined` when no body is parsed (for
example when the request has neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding`,
or when `Content-Type` does not match). In v1, `req.body` was always initialized
to `{}`. Code that assumes `req.body` is always an object should use optional
chaining (for example `req.body?.username`) or set a default.

object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).

`false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.

specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
[bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
to `'100kb'`.

> It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible.   "output_head": "## API

```js
// Import all parsers
const bodyParser = require('body-parser')

// Or import individual parsers directly
const json = require('body-parser/json')
const urlencoded = require('body-parser/urlencoded')
const raw = require('body-parser/raw')
const text = require('body-parser/text')
```

The `bodyParser` object exposes various factories to create middlewares. All
middlewares will populate the `req.body` property with the parsed body when
the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

**Note** As of v2, `req.body` is left `undefined` when no body is parsed (for
example when the request has neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding`,
or when `Content-Type` does not match). In v1, `req.body` was always initialized
to `{}`. Code that assumes `req.body` is always an object should use optional
chaining (for example `req.body?.username`) or set a default.

The various errors returned by this module are described in the
[errors section](#errors).

### bodyParser.json([options])

Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
Unicode encoding of the body.

A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).

#### Options

The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
the following keys:

##### defaultCharset

Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.

##### inflate

When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
`false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.

##### limit

Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
[bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults

const bodyParser = require('body-parser')

// Or import individual parsers directly

The `bodyParser` object exposes various factories to create middlewares. All
middlewares will populate the `req.body` property with the parsed body when
the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

**Note** As of v2, `req.body` is left `undefined` when no body is parsed (for
example when the request has neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding`,
or when `Content-Type` does not match). In v1, `req.body` was always initialized
to `{}`. Code that assumes `req.body` is always an object should use optional
chaining (for example `req.body?.username`) or set a default.

[errors section](#errors).

### bodyParser.json([options])

the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any

A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).

Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not

specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
[bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
to `'100kb'`.

> It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. middlewares will populate the `req.body` property with the parsed body when
the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the

to `'100kb'`.

where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the

either `utf-8` or `iso-8859-1`. Defaults to `utf-8`.

Whether to let the value of the `utf8` parameter take precedence as the charset
selector. It requires the form to contain a parameter named `utf8` with a value

// Or import individual parsers directly

The `bodyParser` object exposes various factories to create middlewares. All
middlewares will populate the `req.body` property with the parsed body when
the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

**Note** As of v2, `req.body` is left `undefined` when no body is parsed (for
example when the request has neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding`,
or when `Content-Type` does not match). In v1, `req.body` was always initialized
to `{}`. Code that assumes `req.body` is always an object should use optional
chaining (for example `req.body?.username`) or set a default.

The various errors returned by this module are described in the
[errors section](#errors).

### bodyParser.json([options])

Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
Unicode encoding of the body.

A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).

#### Options

The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
the following keys:

##### defaultCharset

Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.

##### inflate

When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
`false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.

##### limit

Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
[bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
to `'100kb'`.

> It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.

##### reviver

The `reviver` option is passed directly to `JSON.parse` as the second
argument. You can find more information on this argument
[in the MDN documentation about JSON.parse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/parse#the_reviver_parameter).

##### strict

When set to `true`, it will only accept arrays and objects; when `false`, it will
accept anything `JSON.parse` accepts. Defaults to `true`.

##### type

The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not a
function, `type` option is passed directly to the
[type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
be an extension name (like `json`), a mime type (like `application/json`), or
a mime type with a wildcard (like `*/*` or `*/json`). If a function, the `type`
option is called as `fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy
value. Defaults to `application/json`.

##### verify

The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.

be an extension name (like `urlencoded`), a mime type (like

`*/x-www-form-urlencoded`). If a function, the `type` option is called as
`fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy value. Defaults
to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.

The default charset to parse as, if not specified in content-type. Must be
either `utf-8` or `iso-8859-1`. Defaults to `utf-8`.

##### charsetSentinel

Whether to let the value of the `utf8` parameter take precedence as the charset
selector. It requires the form to contain a parameter named `utf8` with a value
of `✓`. Defaults to `false`.

Whether to decode numeric entities such as `☺` when parsing an iso-8859-1
form. Defaults to `false`.

```js
// Import all parsers
const bodyParser = require('body-parser')

// Or import individual parsers directly
const json = require('body-parser/json')
const urlencoded = require('body-parser/urlencoded')
const raw = require('body-parser/raw')
const text = require('body-parser/text')
```

The `bodyParser` object exposes various factories to create middlewares. All
middlewares will populate the `req.body` property with the parsed body when
the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

**Note** As of v2, `req.body` is left `undefined` when no body is parsed (for
example when the request has neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding`,
or when `Content-Type` does not match). In v1, `req.body` was always initialized
to `{}`. Code that assumes `req.body` is always an object should use optional
chaining (for example `req.body?.username`) or set a default.

The various errors returned by this module are described in the
[errors section](#errors).

### bodyParser.json([options])

Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
Unicode encoding of the body.

A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).

#### Options

The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
the following keys:

##### defaultCharset

Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.

##### inflate

When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
`false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.

##### limit

Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
[bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
to `'100kb'`.

> It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.

##### reviver

The `reviver` option is passed directly to `JSON.parse` as the second
argument. You can find more information on this argument
[in the MDN documentation about JSON.parse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/parse#the_reviver_parameter).

##### strict

When set to `true`, it will only accept arrays and objects; when `false`, it will
accept anything `JSON.parse` accepts. Defaults to `true`.

##### type

The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not a
function, `type` option is passed directly to the
[type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
be an extension name (like `json`), a mime type (like `application/json`), or
a mime type with a wildcard (like `*/*` or `*/json`). If a function, the `type`
option is called as `fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy
value. Defaults to `application/json`.

where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.

```js
// Import all parsers
const bodyParser = require('body-parser')

// Or import individual parsers directly
const json = require('body-parser/json')
const urlencoded = require('body-parser/urlencoded')
const raw = require('body-parser/raw')
const text = require('body-parser/text')
```

The `bodyParser` object exposes various factories to create middlewares. All
middlewares will populate the `req.body` property with the parsed body when
the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

**Note** As of v2, `req.body` is left `undefined` when no body is parsed (for
example when the request has neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding`,
or when `Content-Type` does not match). In v1, `req.body` was always initialized
to `{}`. Code that assumes `req.body` is always an object should use optional
chaining (for example `req.body?.username`) or set a default.

The various errors returned by this module are described in the
[errors section](#errors).

### bodyParser.json([options])

Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
Unicode encoding of the body.

A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).

#### Options

The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
the following keys:

##### defaultCharset

Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.

##### inflate

When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
`false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.

##### limit

Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
[bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
to `'100kb'`.

> It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.

##### reviver

The `reviver` option is passed directly to `JSON.parse` as the second
argument. You can find more information on this argument
[in the MDN documentation about JSON.parse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/parse#the_reviver_parameter).

##### strict

When set to `true`, it will only accept arrays and objects; when `false`, it will
accept anything `JSON.parse` accepts. Defaults to `true`.

##### type

The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not a
function, `type` option is passed directly to the
[type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
be an extension name (like `json`), a mime type (like `application/json`), or
a mime type with a wildcard (like `*/*` or `*/json`). If a function, the `type`
option is called as `fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy
value. Defaults to `application/json`.

The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.

A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`

#### Options

The `urlencoded` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain
any of the following keys:

##### extended

The "extended" syntax allows for rich objects and arrays to be encoded into the

The `parameterLimit` option controls the maximum number of parameters that
are allowed in the URL-encoded data. If a request contains more parameters
than this value, a 413 will be returned to the client. Defaults to `1000`.

parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not
a function, `type` option is passed directly to the
[type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
be an extension name (like `urlencoded`), a mime type (like
`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`), or a mime type with a wildcard (like
`*/x-www-form-urlencoded`). If a function, the `type` option is called as
`fn(req)` and the request is parsed if it returns a truthy value. Defaults
to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

The `verify` option, if supplied, is called as `verify(req, res, buf, encoding)`,
where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.

##### defaultCharset

The default charset to parse as, if not specified in content-type. Must be
either `utf-8` or `iso-8859-1`. Defaults to `utf-8`.

##### charsetSentinel

Whether to let the value of the `utf8` parameter take precedence as the charset
selector. It requires the form to contain a parameter named `utf8` with a value
of `✓`. Defaults to `false`.

##### interpretNumericEntities

Whether to decode numeric entities such as `☺` when parsing an iso-8859-1
form. Defaults to `false`.


##### depth

The `depth` option is used to configure the maximum depth of the `qs` library when `extended` is `true`. This allows you to limit the amount of keys that are parsed and can be useful to prevent certain types of abuse. Defaults to `32`. It is recommended to keep this value as low as possible.

HTTP response code, an `expose` property to determine if the `message` property
should be displayed to the client, a `type` property to determine the type of

The `bodyParser` object exposes various factories to create middlewares. All
middlewares will populate the `req.body` property with the parsed body when
the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

chaining (for example `req.body?.username`) or set a default.

```js
// Import all parsers
const bodyParser = require('body-parser')

// Or import individual parsers directly
const json = require('body-parser/json')
const urlencoded = require('body-parser/urlencoded')

```

The `bodyParser` object exposes various factories to create middlewares. All
middlewares will populate the `req.body` property with the parsed body when
the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

**Note** As of v2, `req.body` is left `undefined` when no body is parsed (for
example when the request has neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding`,
or when `Content-Type` does not match). In v1, `req.body` was always initialized
to `{}`. Code that assumes `req.body` is always an object should use optional
chaining (for example `req.body?.username`) or set a default.

The various errors returned by this module are described in the
[errors section](#errors).

### bodyParser.json([options])

Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
Unicode encoding of the body.

A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).

#### Options

The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
the following keys:

##### defaultCharset

Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.

##### inflate

When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
`false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.

##### limit

Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
[bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
to `'100kb'`.

> It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.

##### reviver

The `reviver` option is passed directly to `JSON.parse` as the second
argument. You can find more information on this argument
[in the MDN documentation about JSON.parse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/parse#the_reviver_parameter).

When set to `true`, it will only accept arrays and objects; when `false`, it will
accept anything `JSON.parse` accepts. Defaults to `true`.

The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not a
function, `type` option is passed directly to the
[type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
be an extension name (like `json`), a mime type (like `application/json`), or

value. Defaults to `application/json`.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "## API

```js
// Import all parsers
const bodyParser = require('body-parser')

// Or import individual parsers directly
const json = require('body-parser/json')
const urlencoded = require('body-parser/urlencoded')
const raw = require('body-parser/raw')
const text = require('body-parser/text')
```

The `bodyParser` object exposes various factories to create middlewares. All
middlewares will populate the `req.body` property with the parsed body when
the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

**Note** As of v2, `req.body` is left `undefined` when no body is parsed (for
example when the request has neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding`,
or when `Content-Type` does not match). In v1, `req.body` was always initialized
to `{}`. Code that assumes `req.body` is always an object should use optional
chaining (for example `req.body?.username`) or set a default.

The various errors returned by this module are described in the
[errors section](#errors).

### bodyParser.json([options])

Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any

the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

```js
// Import all parsers
const bodyParser = require('body-parser')

// Or import individual parsers directly

```

The `bodyParser` object exposes various factories to create middlewares. All
middlewares will populate the `req.body` property with the parsed body when
the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

**Note** As of v2, `req.body` is left `undefined` when no body is parsed (for
example when the request has neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding`,
or when `Content-Type` does not match). In v1, `req.body` was always initialized
to `{}`. Code that assumes `req.body` is always an object should use optional
chaining (for example `req.body?.username`) or set a default.

The various errors returned by this module are described in the
[errors section](#errors).

### bodyParser.json([options])

Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
Unicode encoding of the body.

A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).

#### Options

The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
the following keys:

Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.

`false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.

specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
[bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
to `'100kb'`.

> It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. ```js
// Import all parsers
const bodyParser = require('body-parser')

// Or import individual parsers directly
const json = require('body-parser/json')
const urlencoded = require('body-parser/urlencoded')
const raw = require('body-parser/raw')
const text = require('body-parser/text')
```

The `bodyParser` object exposes various factories to create middlewares. All
middlewares will populate the `req.body` property with the parsed body when
the `Content-Type` request header matches the `type` option.

**Note** As of v2, `req.body` is left `undefined` when no body is parsed (for
example when the request has neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding`,
or when `Content-Type` does not match). In v1, `req.body` was always initialized
to `{}`. Code that assumes `req.body` is always an object should use optional
chaining (for example `req.body?.username`) or set a default.

The various errors returned by this module are described in the
[errors section](#errors).

### bodyParser.json([options])

Returns middleware that only parses `json` and only looks at requests where
the `Content-Type` header matches the `type` option. This parser accepts any
Unicode encoding of the body.

A new `body` object containing the parsed data is populated on the `request`
object after the middleware (i.e. `req.body`).

#### Options

The `json` function takes an optional `options` object that may contain any of
the following keys:

##### defaultCharset

Specify the default character set for the json content if the charset is not
specified in the `Content-Type` header of the request. Defaults to `utf-8`.

##### inflate

When set to `true`, then deflated (compressed) bodies will be inflated; when
`false`, deflated bodies are rejected. Defaults to `true`.

##### limit

Controls the maximum request body size. If this is a number, then the value
specifies the number of bytes; if it is a string, the value is passed to the
[bytes](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bytes) library for parsing. Defaults
to `'100kb'`.

> It’s recommended not to configure a very high limit and to use the default value whenever possible. Allowing larger payloads increases memory usage because of the resources required for decoding and transformations, and it can also lead to longer response times as more data is processed. By ‘very high’, we mean values above the default, for example payloads of 5 MB or more can already start to introduce these risks. With the default limits, these issues do not occur.

##### reviver

The `reviver` option is passed directly to `JSON.parse` as the second
argument. You can find more information on this argument
[in the MDN documentation about JSON.parse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON/parse#the_reviver_parameter).

##### strict

When set to `true`, it will only accept arrays and objects; when `false`, it will
accept anything `JSON.parse` accepts. Defaults to `true`.

##### type

The `type` option is used to determine what media type the middleware will
parse. This option can be a string, array of strings, or a function. If not a
function, `type` option is passed directly to the
[type-is](https://www.npmjs.com/package/type-is#readme) library and this can
be an extension name (like `json`), a mime type (like `application/json`), or
a mime type with a wildcard (like `*/*` or `*/json`). If a function, the `type`

value. Defaults to `application/json`.

where `buf` is a `Buffer` of the raw request body and `encoding` is the
encoding of the request. The parsing can be aborted by throwing an error.
